findings.issue: The phase outcome's margin is met against a per-file cap the phase itself raised per file, not against the 300s cap the outcome and P127.1 name. Windows CI run 38379717433 (544576f) printed test_drive_phase.py at 384.8s (plain 1) and 386.8s (cp1252 1), which is over the old fixed 300s and over the 280s default block timeout; it passes because file_timeout() gives it 1428s from a darwin-recorded cost of 535 slot-seconds times 8 over 3 slots. The same log shows test__deps.py at 259.6s and 268.2s against a 538s timeout (about 2.0x, and run 38370435884 killed it at 300s), so a heavy-file margin of 2x to 3.7x rests on a table nobody has re-recorded from the Windows seconds that now exist. 'Repeated CI runs' is one completed run at this shape; run 38382182020 (1730909c) was still in progress when I read it.
findings.resolution: State the margin against the calibrated timeout in the P127 outcome (drive 3.7x, commit_task_work 69s against its calibrated bound) instead of the fixed 300s, and once run 38382182020 completes re-record the table with `--costs-from-log <saved windows log> --platform win32 --record-costs .github/sweep-costs.json` so deps and drive are weighted by their Windows seconds.

findings.issue: P127.4 made the claim that a stale or partial cost table 'can only cost balance' and 'no longer turns the sweep red'. P127.6 then made the same table set each file's timeout: an entry missing or too low leaves the file at the 300s floor, and 300s is below what test_drive_phase.py needs on Windows (385s). So a stale table can again turn a cell red, through the timeout rather than through a ghost entry. The CONTRIBUTING sentence and sh7/sh9/sh10 describe only the balance half; table_notes() prints nothing about a staged or heavy file with no timed entry.
findings.resolution: Either add a table_notes() note for a staged suite (staged_paths) that has no recorded cost, and reword the CONTRIBUTING sentence to 'costs balance and the length of a hang detector, never which files run'; or give a staged suite a floor of its stage-timeout default times the grant so an unrecorded one is not left at 300s. Add a selftest case for whichever is chosen.

findings.issue: The calibrated timeout for test_drive_phase.py is 1428s (23.8 minutes) and its blocks get 1408s each. A selftests cell has timeout-minutes 25 and about one minute of setup, so a hung drive suite is stopped by the runner's job timeout (the 'cancelled, names no step' outcome the ci.yml header says bounds exist to avoid) rather than named by the sweep. The header also says a bound far above twice the figure is wrong, yet lint (35s) and plugin-validate (14s) have a 5 minute bound.
findings.resolution: Cap file_timeout() at the cell's budget minus setup (for example 15 minutes, still 2.3x the 385s Windows figure) or lower TIMEOUT_PER_COST; if the 5 minute lint and plugin-validate bounds are intended as a floor, say so in the header line.
